day_channel.message: There is no vote on day 1, so no one voted and no one is eliminated.
Night of day 1: player_2 was killed by the wolves last night. Their role is hidden by an illusionist. player_10 was attacked by the serial killer but was saved by the healer!
I watched player_7 last night, and player_5 visited them. That shows a visit, not what player_5 did there.
I’m the Trailseer. I followed player_7 last night, and they visited no one.

player_3, was player_5 the full list of visitors you saw at player_7, or just the visitor you wanted to mention? Your watch is a visit too, so if that was the complete list, it needs explaining; otherwise your result fits player_5’s claim.

I meant player_5 was the visitor my result identified, not that I was claiming a complete list. Since watching is itself a visit, I can’t account for that missing self-entry from what I was given, so don’t treat it as exhaustive; player_5 following player_7 is still consistent with what I saw.

player_3, saying the list wasn’t exhaustive doesn’t resolve the key issue: a watch is a visit, so your own visit to player_7 should have appeared in your result too. Did you actually see yourself listed alongside player_5, or was player_5 the only name you got?

I only saw player_5 listed. You’re right: since watching is a visit, I should have appeared too, and I can’t explain that under the rules. I shouldn’t have called the list non-exhaustive; my result as I reported it is inconsistent, and I can’t honestly give you a better explanation.

Player_5’s claimed follow accounts for why they visited player_7, but it doesn’t explain player_3’s result. Since player_3 confirmed they saw only player_5, their watch claim still conflicts with the rules; I’d make player_3 the leading vote today unless something new changes that picture.

I can’t defend the inconsistency: by the rules, my own watch should have shown me, and it didn’t. The appearance of player_5 in my result doesn’t establish their alignment, so please weigh the contradiction against my claim without treating the result as proof against them.

Separately, the announced Serial Killer attack means player_10 isn’t the SK: an attack on someone night-immune would not be announced. That doesn’t clear them from the wolves, so don’t turn the save into a blanket town read.

One extra rules check: concealment only hides the carrier’s trace at the concealed victim’s door, so it can’t explain a missing self-entry in a watch on player_7. If player_3 was blocked, they wouldn’t have carried out the watch or received that result at all. I’d vote player_3 unless there’s a different explanation that fits those rules.

player_9, that’s right: neither concealment nor a block explains the missing self-entry, and I have no rules-consistent defense for the result I reported. I won’t use it against player_5; the contradiction is evidence against my claim, not proof of player_5’s alignment.

I’d vote player_3 based on the result they’ve admitted they can’t explain. If they’re eliminated, their role is revealed; that gives us a solid check on the claim without treating player_5’s claim as proven either way.

I can’t dispute that my reported watch result breaks the rules, and I understand why you’re voting me. But my elimination isn’t a cost-free check: if I’m telling the truth about being Sentinel, town loses one of its two watches before learning anything further.
Before the vote: player_3 has been accused by player_4, player_6, player_9 and player_8. player_3 gets a last word.

I am the Sentinel, but I can't make that watch result fit the rules: my own visit should have appeared. The honest correction is that the result I reported is unreliable, so it isn't evidence against player_5; if you eliminate me, the role reveal can confirm my role, but it won't explain the contradiction.

The record of player_3, the sentinel: night 1, watched player_7; saw player_5 visit them.

Night of day 2: player_1 was killed by the wolves last night. Their role is hidden by an illusionist. player_6 was stabbed by the serial killer last night. They were a speculator. The Speculator has picked Town.
I was roleblocked last night, so my trail action didn't happen and I have no result.

A roleblock is within the Chanteuse’s toolkit, so it doesn’t make player_5 more suspicious by itself. If the claim is true, they lost a result; I wouldn’t treat that lack of information as a reason to vote them.

Player_5, what did player_7 visit on Night 1 when you followed them? The Sentinel’s record confirms you visited player_7, but your actual follow result would help distinguish a Trailseer claim from just a visit.
I followed player_7 on Night 1, and my result was that they visited no one. The Sentinel's will independently confirms I visited player_7, though that confirms the visit, not my role by itself.

That result gives us a concrete check: the Serial Killer has to visit to make a kill, so if player_7 remembers visiting anyone that night, it would conflict with player_5’s result. player_7, can you say whether you took an action that night, without naming the target?
I didn't visit anyone on Night 1; I held my fire, so player_5's no-visit result is consistent with what I did. That supports this result, but it doesn't confirm they're the Trailseer.

Player_7’s “held my fire” goes beyond saying they didn’t visit; it effectively suggests a Vigilante claim. That makes the no-visit result consistent with their story, but doesn’t verify the role. Player_7, are you claiming Vigilante, and if so, how many shots do you have left?

Yes, I'm the Vigilante, and I have both bullets left. I held fire both nights, so I have no shot result to offer; I saved them because I didn't have a confident target. I’m not going to spend one just to prove the claim—let’s use concrete evidence to narrow a target first.

Here's the vote result for day 3:
  player_4 voted to eliminate player_7
  player_5 voted to eliminate player_7
  player_7 voted to eliminate player_9
  player_8 voted to eliminate player_4
  player_9 voted to eliminate player_8
  player_10 voted to eliminate player_8
It's a tie between ['player_7', 'player_8']. No one is voted out this day.

Night of day 3: player_5 was stabbed by the serial killer last night. They were a trailseer. The record of player_5, the trailseer: night 1, followed player_7; they visited no one; night 2, was roleblocked. player_7 was killed by the wolves last night. They were a vigilante. The record of player_7, the vigilante: night 1, held fire; night 2, held fire.
I’m the Sigilist. I placed my last sigil on player_4 last night, and it had no effect.

That no-effect result doesn’t tell us whether I acted: a sigil can also fail against someone who can’t be killed at night. So it doesn’t clear me, but it isn’t proof that I’m the killer either. We should hear what player_9 and player_10 claim before treating it as a reason to vote anyone.

Player_8’s no-effect result doesn’t clear player_4: if 4 is the Serial Killer, night immunity is exactly why the sigil could fail. I’m unclaimed, but that makes 4 my strongest vote today; the town needs the lone killer gone before the wolves can win.

That makes me a possibility, not a finding; the same no-effect report also fits a target who didn’t attack. One concrete lead we shouldn’t skip is that the GM reported player_10 was attacked by the Serial Killer on night one and saved, so I want their role and account before we lock onto me.

The Night 1 report only establishes that the Serial Killer attacked me and the Healer saved me; it doesn’t establish my role. I’m unclaimed, and I don’t have a verified result to add, so I wouldn’t treat that attack as a reason to clear or condemn anyone.

One hard constraint: player_10 can’t be the Serial Killer—the GM announced the SK attacked them, and attacks on the SK are never announced. Since I’m the Sigilist, that leaves player_4 or player_9 as the SK; my no-effect sigil doesn’t distinguish between them.

Here's the vote result for day 4:

  player_8 voted to eliminate player_4
  player_9 voted to eliminate player_4
  player_10 voted to eliminate player_4
Player player_4 has been voted out and was a serial killer.
Game over! The wolves have won! The speculator lost.
